title.narrative: Advancing Ethiopia’s Oromia Forested Landscape Emission Reductions

description.narrative:
The deforestation rate in Ethiopia has been high the last 50 years, and large investments have been made to change this trend. Several REDD+ projects and programs have been implemented during the last 10 years, Oromia Forest and Landscape Program (OFLP) being one of them. OFLP spans over 32 million hectars , including 9 million hectars of forest, and is a cornerstone of Ethiopia's climate strategy to reduce deforestation and achieve GHG national reductions. OFLP is poised to generate high-integrity juristictional-scale emission reductions (ER) credits, which will be verified by mid-2025. The World Bank has signed an ERPA for 1.8 million credits, but it's exptected that Ethiopia will be able to sell far more than this, and the Government of Ethiopia has requested Norway for support to optimize their sales and increase their capacity in the negotiations with potential buyers.
The Agreement between EDF and Norad aims at supporing the Ethiopian Goverment with transaction advisory experts and legal counsel to navigate the foest carbon market landscape, engage buyers, negotiate fair contracts and execute the sale.
A successful sale will provide Ethiopia with a significant opportunity to catalyze additional financing, with benefits reaching those who contribute to the emiassion reductions, including local communities and the regional and federal government.
